- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next 3–5 days; dampen forecast by 1–3%.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in next 5–7 days.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (1–5 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day moving average of recent prices to anchor forecast.
- For long-term (15+ days) forecasts, model tends to underestimate if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 1–2% buffer based on recent 7-day average sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model often misses downward trends; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
